items.stem: What does two's complement representation make convenient in hardware?

options.text: Subtraction can be performed using the same adder circuitry as addition
options.rationale: Correct: negative numbers are formed so that a single adder handles both add and subtract.
Two's complement is for integers and does not make float division exact.

options.text: It removes the need for a sign bit
options.rationale: The high-order bit still indicates sign in two's complement.
It is a number encoding, unrelated to address space size.

items.explanation: Correct: negative numbers are formed so that a single adder handles both add and subtract.

items.stem: Which statements about the stack in assembly are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: CALL typically pushes a return address onto the stack
options.rationale: Correct: so RET can return to the instruction after the call.

options.text: The stack pointer must be balanced across a procedure to avoid corruption
options.rationale: Correct: unbalanced pushes/pops can overwrite the return address.

options.text: The stack can only hold one value at a time
options.rationale: The stack is a LIFO region holding many values.

options.text: PUSH and POP operate on the program counter directly
options.rationale: They operate on the stack via the stack pointer, not the program counter.

items.explanation: Correct: so RET can return to the instruction after the call.; Correct: unbalanced pushes/pops can overwrite the return address.

items.stem: Why does endianness matter when reading a multi-byte integer from memory?

options.text: It determines whether the most significant byte is stored first or last
options.rationale: Correct: byte order changes how the same bytes are assembled into a value.

options.text: It sets the clock speed of the CPU
options.rationale: Endianness is byte ordering, not clock speed.

options.text: It controls how many registers exist
options.rationale: Register count is independent of endianness.

options.text: It encrypts the value in memory
options.rationale: Endianness is a storage order, not encryption.

items.explanation: Correct: byte order changes how the same bytes are assembled into a value.
